edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults losing weight on GLP-1 receptor agonists
edges.mechanism: Weight loss from GLP-1 agonists comes from reduced energy intake; without enough protein and resistance training, part of the lost tissue is lean mass, which helps explain concern about sarcopenia during aggressive weight reduction.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2026 Abomohsen meta analysis in Can J Diabetes, which suggests that glp-1 receptor agonists tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes for sarcopenia. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
